vocabulary.zh:

vt. 包围, 达到, 图谋, 理解
vocabulary.en:
n. navigational instrument for finding directions
n. the limit of capability
n. drafting instrument used for drawing circles
v. bring about; accomplish
vocabulary.example: If you’re like me, when you pick up a compass you can’t help but spin it this way and that, to see if you can trick it.

vocabulary.zh:

vt. 纺织, 纺, 使旋转, 编造

vocabulary.en:
n. a swift whirling motion (usually of a missile)

vocabulary.zh:

v. withstand the force of something
v. resist immunologically the introduction of some foreign tissue or organ

vocabulary.zh:
n. 实验, 试验, 实验仪器
vi. 实验, 尝试
vocabulary.en:
n. the act of conducting a controlled test or investigation
n. the testing of an idea
n. a venture at something new or different

vocabulary.zh: a. 幽灵一般的, 吓人的, 令人毛骨悚然的

vocabulary.zh: n. 高科技

vocabulary.zh:

vocabulary.en:

n. an event marking a unique or important historical change of course or one on which important developments depend

vocabulary.zh:

vocabulary.zh:

vocabulary.zh:
n. 魔术, 魔法

vocabulary.zh:

vocabulary.example: In modern compasses, a magnetised metal needle has replaced the lodestone spoon.

vocabulary.zh:

vocabulary.zh: a. 古代的, 古老的, 年老的, 旧的

parts.text: Even in today’s high-tech world, compasses are useful navigation tools. A compass works without power, unlike GPS, and in any

and lighting conditions, as opposed to navigation using the Sun, stars or landmarks. If you know which way north is, you can determine any direction.

Like all cool phenomena, the explanation of how a compass works is not magic – it’s

. And people have been making use of this particular aspect of physics for more than 2,000 years.

A lodestone spoon

The earliest versions of the compass were developed in ancient China. They were spoon-shaped and made of lodestones, pieces of the naturally

mineral magnetite.

When allowed to rotate freely, the spoon handle would align itself with a particular direction (north–south). This was used to organise and harmonise environments, as part of a practice you might know as feng shui.

At the time, it was known that some materials were naturally magnetic – able to
one another. However, it wasn’t clear exactly what was causing a compass to align itself north–south until 1600, when English physicist William Gilbert

that Earth itself acted as a giant magnet.

An invisible field

Like all magnets, Earth generates a magnetic field – an invisible region within which its magnetic forces act.

Electricity and magnetism are closely connected. Together, they form one of the fundamental

in physics: electromagnetism. Magnetic fields can be created by electric currents, which are the movements of charged particles; a changing magnetic field can also induce an electrical current.

Our planet spins around an axis once

every 24 hours, which is why we have a night and day cycle. The end points of this axis are the North Pole and the South Pole.

Beneath Earth’s surface, in the outer core, electrically conducting liquid metals circulate in

currents. This movement generates electrical currents. Paired with Earth’s rotation around its axis, these currents maintain a global-scale magnetic field. It extends out into space like a giant, invisible bubble, known as the

.

And it’s this global-scale magnetic field that allows a compass to work.

In modern compasses, a magnetised metal needle has replaced the lodestone spoon. That needle is mounted on a low-friction pivot so it has minimal resistance to the effects of external magnetic fields.

As a result,
there’s a magnet directly nearby, the needle will align itself with Earth’s magnetic north–south direction.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Antarctic microorganisms reveal a rich but often overlooked dimension of biodiversity.
An ancient Arabian lakeshore provides evidence of human life in a landscape once much greener than today.
A new CERN experiment could deepen understanding of the electron and fundamental physics.
A compass works by aligning a magnetised needle with Earth's magnetic field.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Because opposites attract, the “north” arrow on a compass points towards the “south” pole of Earth’s global-scale magnetic field – the area where field lines point down into Earth’s surface.

questions.prompt: What property made lodestone useful in early compasses?
questions.explanation: 第 5 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: They were spoon-shaped and made of lodestones, pieces of the naturally magnetic mineral magnetite.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 11?
options: They were spoon-shaped and made of lodestones, pieces of the naturally magnetic mineral magnetite.
Like all magnets, Earth generates a magnetic field – an invisible region within which its magnetic forces act.
At the time, it was known that some materials were naturally magnetic – able to attract one another.
Our planet spins around an axis once roughly every 24 hours, which is why we have a night and day cycle.
questions.explanation: 定位第 11 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: Our planet spins around an axis once roughly every 24 hours, which is why we have a night and day cycle.
